title: Adapter Identity
description: M9.0 adapter portability contract: an adapter's public descriptor. Declares what an adapter claims to be (adapter_id, adapter_type, brand), which transports it supports, and which contract operations it can perform. DESCRIPTIVE, not cryptographic — trust policy is the enforcement layer for writes; identity says 'this is who I claim to be', trust says 'this is what you may do'. See docs/m9-adapter-pattern.md for the canonical semantic spec.

adapter_id.description: Stable identifier for this adapter instance (e.g. 'claude-web-2026-05-25-operator'). Used by bundles for routing (for_adapter / from_adapter) and by decision-entry / worker-task records for provenance.

adapter_type.description: How the adapter runs — its host class. Distinct from the adapter brand (see `adapter`).

adapter.description: Adapter brand. Aligns with the existing decision-entry and worker-task adapter enums so a single attribution chain works across all writers. Web model brands are supported through operator-mediated bundle/MCP transports unless a local adapter exists.

display_name.description: Human-friendly label (e.g. 'Claude web session', 'Codex local on operator-device').

transport.description: Transports this adapter supports for invoking the contract operations. Multiple is allowed (e.g. a browser extension might support both bundle and a local API).

created_at.description: When this identity descriptor was minted (ISO-8601 UTC). Lets readers detect stale or rotated identities.

Capabilities.description: Per-operation capability declaration. The capability matrix in docs/m9-adapter-pattern.md shows typical values per adapter type.

CapabilityValue.description: true = operation can be performed directly by this adapter; false = unsupported; 'bundle-only' = supported only through an operator-mediated bundle (the adapter cannot reach the layer in real time).
